title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is preparing to convert arbitrary series into continued fractions (E593). On p.138–139 he defines the convergents P/𝔓 of s = a + 1/(b + 1/(c + …)). He observes that each convergent arises from the previous one by replacing the last partial quotient p with p + 1/q. He also notes that the numerator and denominator are multilinear (affine in each index separately) in a, b, …, p.

This page (pp.140–141), step by step:
(1) By multilinearity, P = M + Np and 𝔓 = 𝔐 + 𝔑p, where M, N, 𝔐, 𝔑 do not involve p.
(2) Substituting p → p + 1/q and clearing q gives Q = N + (M+Np)q = N + Pq, and likewise 𝔔 = 𝔑 + 𝔓q.
(3) Substituting q → q + 1/r in Q/𝔔 and clearing r gives R = P + (N + Pq)r = P + Qr, and likewise ℜ = 𝔓 + 𝔔r.
(4) Hence each convergent is formed from the two preceding ones. This is the standard three-term recurrence P_n = a_n P_{n-1} + P_{n-2}, with the same recurrence for denominators.
(5) Initial values are A = a, 𝔄 = 1, B = ab + 1, 𝔅 = b. He tabulates C = Bc + A, D = Cd + B, …, and the same for the Fraktur letters.
(6) Running the recurrence backwards, the numerator term before A must be 1 and the denominator term before 𝔄 must be 0. So the fictitious convergent before the first is 1/0 (modern P_{-1} = 1, Q_{-1} = 0).
(7) §5 begins the difference of consecutive convergents. B/𝔅 − A/𝔄 = (B𝔄 − A𝔅)/(𝔄𝔅); its numerator is A𝔄b + 𝔄 − Ab = 1 because 𝔄 = 1.

The next page continues by induction: the numerators alternate ±1. This leads to the Euler–Wallis identity s = a + Σ(−1)^{n}/(𝔔_{n}𝔔_{n+1}), from which Euler then inverts the process to turn a series into a continued fraction.

The purpose of the page is a self-contained, 'plane and lucid' proof of the well-known convergent recurrence. It serves as the basis for the series ↔ continued-fraction transformation.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.

Small logical gap: the derivation implicitly takes M, N to depend only on a…(previous index) and P to be independent of q. Both hold by construction, and Euler treats Q, 𝔔 as defined by the cleared expressions rather than as reduced fractions, which is legitimate.
The machine transcription has '𝔔 = 𝔑 = (𝔐 + 𝔑p)q'; this should read '𝔔 = 𝔑 + (𝔐 + 𝔑p)q'.

ideas.what: Derivation of the convergent recurrence by the substitution p → p + 1/q and the multilinearity of numerator and denominator in the partial quotients
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental recurrence formulas for continued-fraction convergents (Wallis–Euler recurrence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wallis (Arithmetica infinitorum, 1655), Huygens; systematized by Euler (E71, 1737/1744)
ideas.where_published: E71 'De fractionibus continuis dissertatio'; Introductio in analysin infinitorum vol. I ch. 18; Vollständige Anleitung zur Algebra

ideas.what: Fictitious initial convergent 1/0 obtained by running the recurrence backwards
ideas.modern_name: Initial conditions P_{-1} = 1, Q_{-1} = 0 (matrix product form of convergents)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; implicit in Euler and Lagrange
ideas.where_published: likely implicit in E71 and Introductio ch. 18; unsure of an explicit earlier statement

ideas.what: Difference of consecutive convergents B/𝔅 − A/𝔄 = 1/(𝔄𝔅)
ideas.modern_name: Determinant identity P_n Q_{n-1} − P_{n-1} Q_n = (−1)^{n-1}

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook derivation of the convergent recurrence and its initial conditions, which Euler himself calls the 'regula notissima'. The substitution/multilinearity proof is a pleasant variant but well known. Nothing here is new to the literature.
transcription_corrections: '𝔔 = 𝔑 = (𝔐 + 𝔑p)q' should be '𝔔 = 𝔑 + (𝔐 + 𝔑p)q'.
In the first displayed formula for Q/𝔔, the image reads (Mq + Npq + N)/(𝔐q + 𝔑pq + 𝔑); the transcription is consistent with this.
